lawyer: Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate with Ahmed Sohel, Advocates-For the Petitioners. Shaheed Alam, Advocate—For the Respondent Nos. 2, 3, 5 & 6.
parties:
Abdul Aziz & others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Ministry of Communication and others ----- Respondent
full_judgment: 2. The petitioners in their petition, inter alia, stated that getting appointment in different posts, namely, Wayman, Gate-keeper, Chowkider and Porter under Bangladesh Railway the petitioners have been serving sincerely. There was an agreement between the Ministry of Communication and the leaders of the Sramik Karmachari Sangram Parishad that the service of the temporary employees of the Bangladesh Railway would be regularized after completion of 5 years of their service. On 16-11-2002, the Railway in pursuance of the said agreement absorbed a number of employees against the permanent posts. On 30-5-2000 the office of the Director-General, Bangladesh Railway, Establishment Department-3 issued a letter directing the General Manager of the Railway to prepare a list of the employees who were employed before 16-11-1992. Thereafter-on 22-11-2000 another agreement was effected in between the Bangladesh Railway and the leaders of the Railway Sramik Karmachari Sangram Parishad in presence of the State Minister of Communication. It was agreed that in pursuance of the agreement dated 16-11-1992 the temporary employees of the Railway should be absorbed as permanent employees. In spite of the said agreement the petitioners, who are the temporary employees and have been serving from before 16-11-1992 have not been absorbed. As per direction of the authority a 4-Members Committee was formed to prepare a final list from TLR, Substitutes and Project Employees of the Eastern Zone. The said committee prepared a list of 151 employees including the present petitioners. On 30-5-2003, the Director General of the Railway issued a letter addressing the Secretary, Ministry of Communication recommending to absorb the present petitioners and other temporary workers. On 3-5-2003, the Cabinet Division took decision that after 3 years of service, the temporary employees should be made permanent. Thereafter, by a letter as issued on 2-6-2003 the Ministry of Communication directed the D.G. of Railway to supply the necessary information that how many temporary employees of the Railway had been absorbed/ regularized in the in the revenue budget and how the salaries were paid to the TLR/ substitute the employees of the Project and who was the appointing authority. Accordingly the DG Railway supplied the necessary information. Thereafter, a meeting of the Ministry of Communication was held on 29-4-2004, wherein some conditions were imposed to absorb the temporary employees of Railway in the permanent posts. In pursuance of the letter as issued by the Director General, Bangladesh Railway, the Chief Personal Officer on behalf of the General Manager, Bangladesh Railway, East Zone supplied some information regarding the mode of appointment of temporary employees and the decisions of absorption of some of the employees. The Director-General communicated that information to the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Communication on 23-4-2005. Although 344 temporary employees of the Bangladesh Railway had been absorbed in the permanent posts of the revenue budget and the present petitioners are of similar footings but the respondents did not absorb the petitioners in revenue budget regularizing their service discriminately. The petitioners filed several representations for their absorption but the respondents did not take any positive steps. Lastly the respondents made advertisement as published in the national dailies inviting applications for, fresh appointment for the vacant posts ignoring the agreement as made earlier as mentioned above. Then the petitioners, finding no other alternative, issued notice demanding justice through their learned Advocate, but the respondents did not respond. The petitioners having no other efficacious remedy provided any other law moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.
